title: A small-town house living room, for lives that do not start in a city
missing: The only released home rooms are two city apartments, and the window of each looks out on brick apartment blocks. There is no home interior for a detached house in a small town or the country, so a life in a town of a few thousand opens in a city flat.

consumerSite.playerVisibleUse: The household room shown behind everyday life at home, which is most of play. Seen on a walk in Presque Isle, Maine (about 9,000 people): the home showed a city apartment with brick blocks outside the window.

jurisdiction.reason: The gap is the kind of settlement, not a state: every life outside a large city gets a city apartment today. One ordinary small-town house interior serves towns across the country; regional look is carried by the opening plate, and a window view should show nothing region-specific (a yard, a street of houses, trees), so it does not claim a climate.

whyNeeded: Home is where ordinary life happens, so this is the room most small-town and rural players see most often. A city apartment in a town of 9,000 tells the player the game does not know where they live.
requestedBy: art bench and regional scenes thread
notes: Selection today: resolveLifeScene picks one of DOMESTIC_SCENE_IDS by hashing the household id, and both are apartments. Once this plate is released, the selector needs to prefer it for households in small places; that is a code change after the art exists, not a reason to hold the request.
First person, like every room: no people drawn in. Present household members are rendered separately.
The window should show a neighboring house, yard or trees in a season-neutral way, or be curtained, so one plate does not stand for July and January at once.
Not in scope: the housemate drawn as a dark placeholder shape in the same walk. That is the modular people figure, which has its own owner.
